  PROBLEM: The greedy URL/path tail consumes adjacent issue links as one match, so downstream extraction keeps the first issue number and silently omits subsequent issues.
  WHY: Adjacent Markdown or comma-separated issue references without whitespace can therefore be missed by callers that rely on this helper, including status updates and review metadata.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1672-1673 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The comment incorrectly says consuming a Markdown link's closing parenthesis is harmless, although the tail can continue across Markdown delimiters and swallow adjacent issue links.
  WHY: The comment inaccurately documents the behavior that causes adjacent links to be swallowed.
- tests/test_issue_pr_status_comment_url_links.py:126-144 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The tests do not cover adjacent repo-scoped issue URLs without intervening whitespace, leaving the greedy-tail regression undetected by CI.
  WHY: Existing multi-URL cases use whitespace or words as separators, so CI can pass while the helper drops an issue from adjacent links.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1689-1690 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `grep -viE 'issues/[0-9]+.*#$'` filter only drops matches that end in `#`, so it does not reliably filter widened-tail matches that end in other characters.
  WHY: A query-shaped URL match ending in a non-`#` character can pass the filter, making its narrow behavior a load-bearing assumption.
- changelog.d/5776-ignore-comment-url-issue-links.md:10 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The “Still counted” row claims query-string issue URLs are counted, but adjacent URLs with query strings can cause the second issue reference to be omitted.
  WHY: The documented user-facing claim does not match the helper’s behavior for adjacent URLs.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1690 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The greedy tail consumes sibling issue URLs when adjacent Markdown links or repo-scoped URLs have no whitespace, `<`, `>`, or `#` delimiter, so `grep -oE` emits a match spanning both URLs and `sed` keeps only the first issue number.
  WHY: A PR body containing `[one](https://github.com/shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/issues/1?q=1),[two](https://github.com/shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/issues/2)` returns `[1]` instead of `[1, 2]`.

TASK_GAP
Requirement: The plan (implementation step 2) lists "bare URLs, paths, and keyword refs still match, including mixed text" as a test case, and Copilot review comment entry[18] requests "an adjacent queried/trailing-slash Markdown-link regression case." The plan's Goals state that bare `/issues/N` URLs are unchanged and that the helper correctly handles "mixed text."
Expected change site: tests/test_issue_pr_status_comment_url_links.py, the `test_bare_urls_paths_and_closing_keywords_still_link` function and a sibling test covering adjacent URLs without whitespace
Evidence of absence: `test_bare_urls_paths_and_closing_keywords_still_link` (lines 132-144) tests two URLs with whitespace between them (` and https://...`) but no test exercises `[one](.../issues/1?q=1),[two](.../issues/2)` where the comma and second URL are consumed by the greedy tail. The pass-1 cross-pollination flagged this gap, and the Copilot comment entry[18] requests the exact adjacent-queried Markdown-link regression case.
SEVERITY: MAJOR

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1690-1691 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The greedy URL/path tail consumes adjacent issue links into one match, so `sed` truncates to the first issue; when an adjacent URL contains a `#` fragment, the resulting match can instead be discarded entirely by the filter.
  WHY: Callers can miss valid linked issues in PR descriptions, leading to missed status transitions and unfinalized issue lineages.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1672-1673 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The comment incorrectly says a Markdown link's closing parenthesis is harmless, although the tail can continue through Markdown delimiters and swallow adjacent issue links.
  WHY: The inaccurate comment documents and rationalizes the behavior that causes adjacent Markdown links to be swallowed.
- tests/test_issue_pr_status_comment_url_links.py:126-138 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test function `test_bare_urls_paths_and_closing_keywords_still_link` does not test adjacent issue URLs or Markdown links with query parameters or trailing slashes and no whitespace separator.
  WHY: CI does not enforce this edge case, allowing the greedy-tail regression to pass undetected.

TASK_GAP
Requirement: The PR description and plan specify that bare repo-scoped issue URLs and paths must continue to link ("Bare /issues/N URLs and paths, and close|fix|resolve keyword references, are unchanged"), and regression tests must pin that all valid linked issues are properly extracted.
Expected change site: tests/test_issue_pr_status_comment_url_links.py in test_bare_urls_paths_and_closing_keywords_still_link and scripts/gh_helpers.sh line 1690
Evidence of absence: tests/test_issue_pr_status_comment_url_links.py lacks any test asserting that adjacent issue URLs or Markdown links without intervening whitespace (e.g. [one](https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/1?q=1),[two](https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/2)) both extract successfully, which allowed the regression where the second issue reference is swallowed to go undetected.
SEVERITY: MAJOR

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1689-1690 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The tail class does not exclude commas or parentheses, so a URL with a query or path tail can greedily cross Markdown link boundaries and swallow the next link; downstream filtering and `sed` then retain only the first issue number.
  WHY: Callers of this helper can silently drop a valid second linked issue in adjacent bare repo-scoped URLs.
- scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1689-1690 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `grep -viE 'issues/[0-9]+.*#$'` filter only drops matches that end in `#`, so a widened-tail match ending in another character can pass the filter.
  WHY: A query-shaped URL match ending in a non-`#` character can pass, making the filter’s narrow reach a load-bearing assumption.
- changelog.d/5776-ignore-comment-url-issue-links.md:10 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The “Still counted” row claims query-string issue URLs are counted, but adjacent URLs with query strings can cause the second issue reference to be omitted.
  WHY: The user-facing claim does not match the helper’s behavior for adjacent URLs.

TASK_GAP
Requirement: The plan's Goals state "Bare `/issues/N` URLs and paths, and `close|fix|resolve` keyword references, are unchanged." The PR description promises the helper still returns "bare repo-scoped `/issues/<n>` URLs." Copilot's inline review at comment 4152171444 (entry[18]) asks for an adjacent queried/trailing-slash Markdown-link regression case.
Expected change site: scripts/gh_helpers.sh (the tail regex group on line 1689-1690) and tests/test_issue_pr_status_comment_url_links.py (a new case alongside `test_bare_urls_paths_and_closing_keywords_still_link`).
Evidence of absence: `test_bare_urls_paths_and_closing_keywords_still_link` (lines 132-144 of the new test module) covers `https://github.com/<repo>/issues/9/ and https://github.com/<repo>/issues/10?x=1` and `[t](https://github.com/<repo>/issues/14?a=5).`, but the only multi-URL assertions separate the URLs with whitespace or wrap one in Markdown. No test asserts that `[one](https://github.com/<repo>/issues/1?q=1),[two](https://github.com/<repo>/issues/2)` returns `[1, 2]` — and the current regex returns `[1]`. Round 3's new `test_fragment_after_parentheses_in_the_tail_is_not_a_link` exercises only single URLs and one accept case with ` and ` separator; the regression shape Copilot named is not pinned anywhere in `ci.yml`.
